title: The Guarded Line: What Metacircular Proof Theory and Self-Model Dynamics Share
description: Formal calculi capable of hosting their own reduction divide by a clean triangle. In the hosted case, reduction terminates: cut elimination for sequent calculi, normalization for natural deduction, strong normalization for the simply typed λ-calculus. Under self-application through the untyped fixpoint, termination is lost; the system can always take one more step and need never deliver anything. With the guarded fixpoint — recursion through the later modality — termination is deliberately given up and replaced by something better behaved: productivity, one constructor per interval. Dynamical systems that represent their own states divide by a corresponding triangle: dissolution (reduction to a normal form carried by a host), the retention loop (self-examination kept in play, converging on a holdable self-representation), and the interval structure that keeps self-examination stable instead of divergent. This paper states, as a thesis with a proof sketch, a structural correspondence between the two triangles, and traces the single line that runs through all three vertices — the guarded line: in proof theory the later modality, in the dynamics the interval. The formal side is developed with machine-checked anchors in a companion Lean 4 mechanization of a sorted linear λ-calculus with guarded recursion; the dynamical side is developed from a control-theoretic model of self-monitoring systems whose thresholds are derived and unfitted. The correspondence types the self-model as a lens rather than a noun (guarded machinery, sustained one interval at a time), assigns the model's thresholds the role of semantic values — dynamical denotations of proof-theoretic distinctions — and predicts nothing about any mind. The paper closes with structural analyses of historical figures who reached self-reference without metacircular representation and were held by external containers: the evidence that the correspondence is not a restatement of the contemplative literature it must be distinguished from.
